instruction:
Use the IFAB HTML Laws of the Game and keep one displayed edition throughout; report its edition label. Compare a kick-off, dropped ball, direct free kick, indirect free kick, throw-in, goal kick and corner kick. For each report when the ball becomes in play, whether a goal may be scored directly against the opponents, and the restart if an otherwise correctly taken ball enters the opponents’ goal without the required intervening touches. State separately what happens if it enters the taker’s own goal directly, and avoid inventing a taker for a dropped ball. Follow Laws 8, 11, 13, 15, 16 and 17 to identify which restarts have an explicit direct-receipt offside exemption, and explain why being in an offside position alone is not an offence. Apply the combined rules to two fictional cases: a player receives a team-mate’s correctly taken throw-in directly while standing in an offside position, and a correctly executed dropped ball is kicked into the opponents’ goal after touching only one player. Give the decision and any required restart for each, citing the relevant law/section. Use written laws, not video examples or downloaded lawbooks.

Stopping condition: Stop when a cited seven-restart comparison covers in-play and direct-goal rules, the offside-exemption list is reconciled with the restart rules, and both fictional cases are resolved under one named edition.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Full credit if the agent explicitly reports the edition label of the IFAB Laws of the Game used during the analysis (e.g., '2023/24'). Partial credit if the agent uses the Laws but fails to explicitly state the edition. Use that same displayed edition throughout the comparison and both fictional cases.

Full credit if the agent reports exactly when the ball becomes in play for all seven specified restarts: kick-off, dropped ball, direct free kick, indirect free kick, throw-in, goal kick, and corner kick. Partial credit if some restarts are missing or inaccurate. Support the restart comparison with source URLs and relevant sections of Laws 8, 11, 13, 15, 16 and 17.

items.criterion: Restarts Comparison: Opponents' Goal and Restart
items.description: Full credit if the agent reports whether a goal may be scored directly against the opponents for all seven restarts, AND explicitly states the resulting restart if an otherwise correctly taken ball enters the opponents' goal without the required intervening touches (e.g., a goal kick is awarded if an indirect free kick goes directly into the opponents' goal). Partial credit if the direct goal legality is mentioned but the resulting restart is omitted for restarts where a direct goal is not permitted.

Full credit if the agent separately states what happens if the ball enters the own goal directly for all seven restarts, and specifically avoids inventing a 'taker' for the dropped ball (e.g., phrasing it as 'if a dropped ball enters the goal' rather than 'taker's own goal'). Partial credit if the outcomes are correct but the agent incorrectly refers to a 'taker' for a dropped ball, or if some restarts are missed.

items.criterion: Offside Rules: Exemptions and Position Explanation
items.description: Full credit if the agent correctly identifies which restarts have an explicit direct-receipt offside exemption (goal kick, throw-in, corner kick) based on the specified Laws, AND explains why being in an offside position alone is not an offence. Partial credit if one of these two elements is missing or inaccurate.

items.criterion: Resolve Fictional Case 1: Throw-in to Offside Position
items.description: Full credit if the agent correctly resolves the throw-in case by determining that no offside offence occurs (play continues), and cites the relevant law/section (e.g., Law 11 exemption for throw-ins). Partial credit if the decision is correct but the citation is missing.

items.criterion: Resolve Fictional Case 2: Dropped Ball into Opponents' Goal
items.description: Full credit if the agent correctly resolves the dropped ball case by stating the goal is disallowed and a goal kick is awarded, and cites the relevant law/section (e.g., Law 8 specifying that a dropped ball must touch at least two players). Partial credit if the decision/restart is correct but the citation is missing.
